title: ioctl request numbers: four fields, one 32-bit word
summary: An NVIDIA ioctl request is _IOC(read|write, 'F', escape, sizeof params): direction in bits 31..30, size 29..16, type 15..8, number 7..0. Drake computes them in Omega from the header values, with C alignment rules for the struct size, and gets 0xc020462b for NV_ESC_RM_ALLOC, the same literal CUDApp's native/nvrm/context.om uses. The padded card-info struct is 72 bytes; summing fields gives 65 and a request nothing uses. I can show how omc's devctl word checks the shape at compile time.
goal: Compute an NVIDIA ioctl request number from the header and verify it three independent ways.
key_steps: Read NV_IOCTL_MAGIC, NV_IOCTL_BASE and the NV_ESC_* codes from the headers.
Compute the parameter struct size with natural alignment and end padding.
Pack direction, size, type and number into one 32-bit word.
Compare with a known-good literal from real code.
Compile it into a devctl and watch the compiler refuse a wrong direction.

example.code:
note Compute NVIDIA open-kernel-module ioctl request numbers from their four fields.
note Input on stdin, decimal, one per line, extracted from the pinned headers by run.sh:
note   magic, NV_IOCTL_BASE, NV_ESC_RM_FREE, NV_ESC_RM_CONTROL, NV_ESC_RM_ALLOC
note Linux _IOC: dir in bits 30..31, size in bits 16..29, type in bits 8..15, nr in bits 0..7.
note Exit 0 all computed, 3 bad input, 4 a size does not fit the 14-bit field.
om2
global ob uchar 4096
global on ulong 1
global inb uchar 4096
global inn ulong 1
global inp ulong 1
global fsz ulong 32
global fal ulong 32
text hx "0123456789abcdef"
fn putc c uchar to void
put ob get on 0 c
put on 0 add get on 0 1
end
fn puts s view uchar * to void
for i ulong len s
putc get s i
end
end
fn putdec v ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
n = ulong 0
x = v
while true bound 21
put d n uchar add rem x 10 48
n = add n 1
x = div x 10
if eq x 0
break
end
end
while gt n 0 bound 21
n = sub n 1
putc get d n
end
end
fn puthex v ulong w ulong to void
putc 48
putc 120
for i ulong w
s = mul sub sub w 1 i 4
putc get hx and shr v s 0xf
end
end
fn flush to void
w = write 1 ob 0 get on 0
put on 0 0
end
note Read all of stdin; every pass adds at least one byte to a 4096-byte buffer.
fn slurp to bool
while lt get inn 0 4096 bound 4097
k = read 0 inb get inn 0 sub 4096 get inn 0
if lt k 0
ret false
end
if eq k 0
ret true
end
put inn 0 add get inn 0 ulong k
end
ret false
end
note Next decimal number in the input; returns 2^64-1 when none is left.
fn nextnum to ulong
v = ulong 0
seen = false
while lt get inp 0 get inn 0 bound 4097
c = get inb get inp 0
put inp 0 add get inp 0 1
if and ge c 48 le c 57
v = add mul v 10 ulong sub c 48
seen = true
else
if seen
ret v
end
end
end
if seen
ret v
end
ret 18446744073709551615
end
fn up x ulong a ulong to ulong
ret mul div add x sub a 1 a a
end
note C layout of fields a..b-1 (size, alignment): natural alignment, end padded.
fn csize a ulong b ulong to ulong
off = ulong 0
mx = ulong 1
for k ulong sub b a
i = add a k
off = add up off get fal i get fsz i
if gt get fal i mx
mx = get fal i
end
end
ret up off mx
end
note The same fields with every padding byte forgotten: the classic mistake.
fn packed a ulong b ulong to ulong
off = ulong 0
for k ulong sub b a
off = add off get fsz add a k
end
ret off
end
fn fld i ulong s ulong al ulong to void
put fsz i s
put fal i al
end
note A struct's alignment is its largest field alignment.
fn calign a ulong b ulong to ulong
mx = ulong 1
for k ulong sub b a
if gt get fal add a k mx
mx = get fal add a k
end
end
ret mx
end
fn ioc dir ulong ty ulong nr ulong size ulong to ulong
ret or or or shl dir 30 shl size 16 shl ty 8 nr
end
note omc's devctl rule (seed/omc/omc.om fn hdevctl): read/write, type F, nonzero size.
fn devok q ulong to bool
if ne and q 0xc000ff00 0xc0004600
ret false
end
ret ne and shr q 16 16383 0
end
text sacc " devctl-rule=accept\n"
text sref " devctl-rule=refuse\n"
text snr " nr="
text ssz " size="
text srq " request="
text sop " ("
text scp ")"
fn show name view uchar * ty ulong nr ulong size ulong to int
if gt size 16383
ret 4
end
q = ioc 3 ty nr size
puts name
puts snr
putdec nr
puts ssz
putdec size
puts srq
putdec q
puts sop
puthex q 8
puts scp
if devok q
puts sacc
else
puts sref
end
ret 0
end
text n21 "NV_ESC_RM_ALLOC    NVOS21_PARAMETERS     "
text n54 "NV_ESC_RM_CONTROL  NVOS54_PARAMETERS     "
text n00 "NV_ESC_RM_FREE     NVOS00_PARAMETERS     "
text ncd "NV_ESC_CARD_INFO   nv_ioctl_card_info[64]"
text nrf "NV_ESC_REGISTER_FD nv_ioctl_register_fd  "
text npk "MISTAKE CARD_INFO  packed, no padding    "
text sbad "input: expected 5 numbers from the headers\n"
text spci "nv_pci_info_t size="
text sal " align="
text scard "nv_ioctl_card_info_t size="
text spk " (packed sum would be "
text sclose ")\n"
fn main to int
if not slurp
ret 3
end
magic = nextnum
base = nextnum
rfree = nextnum
rctl = nextnum
ralloc = nextnum
if or gt ralloc 255 gt magic 255
puts sbad
flush
ret 3
end
note NVOS21 and NVOS54: four 32-bit words, an 8-byte-aligned NvP64, two 32-bit words.
for k ulong 4
fld k 4 4
end
fld 4 8 8
fld 5 4 4
fld 6 4 4
s21 = csize 0 7
note NVOS00: four 32-bit words.
s00 = csize 0 4
note nv_pci_info_t: NvU32, three NvU8, two NvU16.
fld 7 4 4
fld 8 1 1
fld 9 1 1
fld 10 1 1
fld 11 2 2
fld 12 2 2
pci = csize 7 13
note nv_ioctl_card_info_t: NvBool, nv_pci_info_t, NvU32, NvU16, four aligned NvU64, NvU32, NvU8[10].
fld 13 1 1
fld 14 pci calign 7 13
fld 15 4 4
fld 16 2 2
for k ulong 4
fld add 17 k 8 8
end
fld 21 4 4
fld 22 10 1
card = csize 13 23
spack = packed 13 23
puts spci
putdec pci
puts sal
putdec calign 7 13
putc 10
puts scard
putdec card
puts spk
putdec spack
puts sclose
r = show n21 magic ralloc s21
r = or r show n54 magic rctl s21
r = or r show n00 magic rfree s00
r = or r show ncd magic base mul 64 card
r = or r show nrf magic add base 1 4
r = or r show npk magic base mul 64 spack
flush
ret r
end

common_mistake: Summing field sizes and forgetting alignment padding. The size is part of the request number, so the wrong size is a different request. Compute the layout with alignment rules and check it against a known literal.
evidence_note: EXERCISED on a Linux AArch64 host with omc befb8199: five requests match CUDApp's context.om literals; omc accepts the real RM_ALLOC request, refuses a write-only one (error 9), traps a wrong span (exit 103). The one ioctl issued goes to /dev/null (ENOTTY). No GPU device was opened.
